title: Calibrated Test-Time Guidance for Bayesian Inference
claim: Common guidance approximations yield miscalibrated samples that miss the true posterior; our estimator matches it, including under tempering where gradient rescaling fails.
layout: 2 groups of 2x2 small-multiple density plots, divided by vertical line, blue vs orange
description: Eight small 1-D density plots in two 2x2 blocks separated by a vertical line. In the left block, panels are titled Diffusion Posterior (ours), Posterior Mean (DPS), Gaussian Approximation (ΠGDM) and Optimization (NDTM). Each plots a green bimodal prior, a red sigmoid likelihood, a blue true posterior curve and histograms of samples. In our panel the blue histogram sits exactly on the posterior. In the baseline panels the orange histograms are shifted, too narrow or too spiky. The right block shows guidance scale γ = 1, 2, 4 and 8. Blue histograms from our scaled likelihood follow the tempered posterior. Orange scaled-gradient histograms drift to the right and become biased as γ grows. The eye goes first to the blue/orange overlap.
caption: We present a test-time guidance scheme to sample from calibrated Bayesian posteriors. (Left) Our framework accurately samples the correct posterior {\color{C0}(blue)}. Posterior mean ([ref]), posterior Gaussian ([ref]), and optimal control approximations ([ref]) to the diffused likelihood $p(y \mid x_t)$ yield uncalibrated samples {\color{C1}(orange)}. (Right) Our framework can correctly sample from tempered posteriors $p(x \mid y, \gamma) \propto p(x) p(y \mid x)^\gamma$ {\color{C0}(blue)}. Rescaling the noisy gradient by $\gamma$ leads to biased samples, even if the diffused likelihood $p(y \mid x_t)$ is accurately estimated {\color{C1}(orange)}.
abstract: Test-time guidance is a widely used mechanism for steering pretrained diffusion models toward outcomes specified by a reward function. Existing approaches, however, focus on maximizing reward rather than sampling from the true Bayesian posterior, leading to miscalibrated inference. In this work, we show that common test-time guidance methods do not recover the correct posterior distribution and identify the structural approximations responsible for this failure. We then propose consistent alternative estimators that enable calibrated sampling from the Bayesian posterior. We significantly outperform previous methods on a set of Bayesian inference tasks, and set a new state-of-the-art PSNR in black hole image reconstruction.
